key_test: Pearson chi-square without Yates correction, options (two/ten) x decision (confirming/disconfirming), focus == 'control' only; d from phi
exclusions: drop rows with blank decision (no answer on the choice; 27 rows, identical to the audit script's 27 listed session ids); aware-of-hypothesis participants already removed in the SAS build (none of its 30 listed ids remain); then keep focus == control

r_script.why: package missing: sas7bdat (no SAS reader; haven also missing), dplyr, gmodels; effsize present but unused

python.es: phi = 0.2175; d = 0.4456 by 2phi/sqrt(1-phi^2); 0.4566 by the script's 2phi/(1-phi^2)

agreement: Python and table agree on chi2 7.095 vs 7.10, p .0077 vs .008, N 150. R absent for this script (packages missing). The table's d = .46 follows the script's non-standard conversion 2r/(1-r^2); the standard 2r/sqrt(1-r^2) gives .446
notes: Anchored on the table statistic and the final report (X2(1, N=150)=7.10, p=.008; 59% vs 79% confirming at two vs ten options, reproduced: 46/78 and 57/72). The script's comment calls the 27 ids participants who 'did not know answer' to the DV; they are exactly the blank-decision rows. The report says 25 aware participants were removed, the SAS build lists 30 ids; neither count changes the posted file, which already lacks all 30.
